summary: Completed comprehensive testing of context-dependent sort defaulting feature. All 12 test scenarios passed with 100% success rate. The sort logic correctly defaults to 'newest' when browsing without filters, switches to 'price_asc' when a make or model is selected, and respects user manual overrides that stick through taxonomy changes. Clear all properly resets behavior. All regression checks passed including 16 listings per page on both desktop and mobile, translated filter chip labels, TrustStrip positioning, and car detail page functionality.
passed_tests: Fresh page load defaults to 'newest' sort with no filters applied
Selecting a make (Mercedes-Benz) automatically switches sort to 'price_asc' with prices in ascending order
Manual sort override to 'year_desc' STICKS when taxonomy selection changes (different model selected)
Manual sort override STICKS when model is cleared back to 'All models'
Clear all button resets sort to 'newest' and clears all filters
Automatic sort behavior re-enabled after clear all (selecting make again switches to 'price_asc')
Removing make chip via X button returns sort to 'newest'
Page navigation resets to page 1 when sort changes
Desktop displays exactly 16 car listings per page (data-testid='car-row')
Mobile displays exactly 16 car listings per page (data-testid='car-card')
Applied filter chips show translated labels (e.g., 'Make: Mercedes-Benz') with no Korean Hangul characters
TrustStrip with trust badges (Verified history, Inspection, Insurance records) positioned above taxonomy selects
Car detail page loads successfully with photos, specifications, equipment, inspection, and insurance history
No console errors on detail page
Mobile filter button (data-testid='open-filters-button') exists and accessible
